method: Traced every authority in CoreDeps through both its interface and production implementation side, then tested the suite against retry identity, provider/scanner/Probe execution, cancellation, storage contention, and process supervision. Distinguished direct ambient access from use of an explicit injected capability port.

priorClosureAssessment.A2-R1-V11-01: NOT CLOSED: the boundary is listed, but filesystem/store/provider/supervisor placement is internally inconsistent and full Plan execution is not representable by the API.
priorClosureAssessment.A2-R1-V11-02: PARTIAL: LN-02 no longer overclaims listed-field completeness, but LN-11/LN-12 still overclaim global exhaustiveness from a static closure plus representative runtime path.
priorClosureAssessment.A2-R1-V11-03: CLOSED AT SPECIFICATION LEVEL: LN-06 now holds authoritative inputs equal and varies only disposable acceleration.
priorClosureAssessment.A2-R1-V11-04: CLOSED AT SPECIFICATION LEVEL: LN-09 now permits typed bounded contention rather than asserting both writers succeed.
priorClosureAssessment.A2-R1-06.signatureDefect: CLOSED NARROWLY: StoreHandle has one parameter path; this does not close the authority/closure problem.

resolves.B-R1V12-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: LN-13 requires identical ExecutionId for identical inputs although ExecutionId is per-attempt, allocated outside the core, and must distinguish retries/concurrency.
resolves.B-R1V12-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: explicit absence of all filesystem access conflicts with injected snapshotAccess/storeHandle and LN-11 cannot both traverse production implementations and find no filesystem.
resolves.B-R1V12-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: the API cannot execute a validated Plan containing scanner/provider/probe work because supervision is outside, observations are not an input, and no supervisor capability exists.
resolves.B-R1V12-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: LN-07's orphan-process assertion is vacuous in a core forbidden from spawning/supervising child processes; LN-09 tests storage protocol, not lifetime neutrality.
resolves.B-R1V12-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: LN-11 plus one representative LN-12 run cannot conclude exhaustive absence of dynamic, native, transitive, injected, or unexecuted ambient paths.
resolves.B-R1V12-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: analyze(...)->SealedRun has no typed failure/cancel/indeterminate/publication result and lets the core seal despite host-owned finalization.
resolves.B-R1V12-07: OPEN-BLOCKER: PO-01 unconditionally mandates one-shot deployment while R-1 says only item (1) is closable without measurement.

evidence: architecture/02 defines ExecutionId as per-attempt
C-2 v2 allocates ExecutionId during outer admission work
executionCoreBoundary says admission is outside the core
LN-13 says the core produces identical RunId/ExecutionId for identical inputs
findings.impact: Retries and concurrent identical requests collide, and the core mints an identity owned by admission.
findings.requiredChange: Inject an already allocated unique ExecutionId as attempt metadata and prove it does not affect EvidenceDigest. If a content-derived Run/Evidence identity is needed, define it separately. LN-13 should vary unique ExecutionIds over identical semantic inputs and assert equal EvidenceDigest, not equal attempt IDs.

evidence: coreDeps includes snapshotAccess and storeHandle
coreApi.explicitlyAbsent forbids filesystem access of any kind
production snapshot/CAS/SQLite implementations necessarily access filesystem
LN-11 import/call closure forbids any reachable filesystem API
knownLimitations admits the StoreHandle boundary is unresolved
findings.impact: Either every real core fails LN-11/LN-12 or the analysis stops at an interface and no longer proves the production authority claim.
findings.requiredChange: Define boundary-aware capability rules: direct ambient imports/calls are forbidden; calls through explicit snapshot/store ports are allowed and semantically scoped. Analyze the core package to the port boundary, then separately conformance-test each production adapter's authority. Do not claim 'no filesystem access of any kind.'

evidence: ValidatedPlan can contain fact derivation, scanners/providers, and Probe stages
external process supervision is outside the core
the core receives Probe observations as inputs according to prose, but analyze(snapshot, plan, deps) has no observations input or supervisor
providerRegistry is inside deps, potentially pulling provider ambient/process authority back into core closure
findings.impact: The core either cannot execute the full Plan or secretly relies on an unlisted callback/orchestration authority, invalidating lifetime-neutrality tests.
findings.requiredChange: Choose a factoring: an orchestration host executes effectful/provider stages and passes a sealed StageInput/ObservationSet into a pure evaluation core, or the execution core receives a typed supervisor port and includes its behavior in the boundary. Specify sequencing, identities, Coverage, and cancellation for that choice.

evidence: LN-07 requires no orphan child process
the core is forbidden from process spawn and supervision
LN-09 exercises multi-process ledger/CAS behavior owned by storage/host protocol rather than core lifetime discrimination
findings.impact: The suite can pass lifetime-neutral core code without testing the host behavior it claims, while unrelated storage failures can fail the core decision.
findings.requiredChange: Split suites: core re-entrancy/ambient-authority, host lifecycle/cancellation/supervision, and storage multi-process integrity. Keep cross-suite composition acceptance but do not use vacuous assertions to close R-1(1).

evidence: LN-11 covers the statically modeled import/call graph
LN-12 executes one representative Plan
dynamic loading, FFI/native libraries, reflection, generated code, injected implementations, and unexecuted branches can evade one or both
the history explicitly warns against deriving a global claim from local form
findings.impact: The artifact again calls the dependency set exhaustive when its instruments provide bounded evidence only.
findings.requiredChange: State the analysis boundary and completeness limits. Combine dependency-policy enforcement, binary/link inspection where applicable, restricted runtime tests across capability-specific Plans, and negative mutations. Treat unmodeled dynamic/native paths as TCB or deny them by construction.

evidence: coreApi returns SealedRun only
D9 requires operational, interrupted, indeterminate, and request-rejected outcomes
architecture/07 gives host finalizer sole termination construction and authoritative publication can fail after semantic completion
findings.impact: Cancellation, provider faults, missing Coverage, busy timeout, and commit failure have no truthful return value, or the core oversteps host-owned seal/publication.
findings.requiredChange: Return a typed CoreCompletion/DraftRunContribution union with findings, exact Coverage, diagnostics references, and typed faults/cancellation. Let the host publication/finalization layer seal the authoritative Run and map termination.

evidence: R-1 says only core lifetime-neutrality is closable now
PO-01 says a full-capability one-shot host must exist
CI/offline/recovery are requirements but do not logically select process-per-command topology
findings.impact: A product/deployment choice is preserved as an obligation outside the suite, bypassing the reopened status rather than resolving it.
findings.requiredChange: Remove PO-01 from this conformance artifact or mark it as a separate candidate requiring R-1 measurement/product adjudication. State topology-neutral CI/offline/recovery requirements instead.
findings.confidence: high on status mismatch; medium on eventual product choice

sealedPropertiesCovered.assessment: Not closed; the boundary and identity model remain contradictory.
LN-09 is directionally corrected but belongs to a storage protocol suite.
LN-06 now tests the right cache-only variation at specification level.
LN-05/LN-06 preconditions are aligned; LN-13 contradicts per-attempt identity.
Static closure plus representative runtime does not prove global absence across injected/production adapters.

knownLimitations: No concrete host/core module graph exists, so the review cannot select exact static-analysis boundaries; it demonstrates why the present universal boundary cannot work.
LN-06 and LN-09 are accepted only as conformance specifications, not demonstrated tests.
This review does not settle R-1 items (2)-(4) or choose a one-shot/resident product topology.
whatWouldChangeOverallVerdict: A v1.3 that keeps ExecutionId unique and outside the core, defines allowed injected ports versus forbidden ambient access, can represent the full Plan or narrows the core honestly, splits host/storage tests from core neutrality, bounds closure claims, returns a typed non-sealed completion, and removes the unadjudicated one-shot obligation.
